name: Vitamin E gummies

lead: Vitamin E gummies are chewable supplements containing vitamin E, a fat-soluble antioxidant. They became a skincare trend on social media, where people take them hoping for better-looking skin.

Vitamin E has been studied for skin health and ageing, though most studies found limited or inconclusive benefits [1]. Gummies are a convenient form of the same nutrient found in nuts, seeds and oils.

paras: People take them as a daily supplement, often alongside other beauty gummies. They are an oral route, different from vitamin E oils or creams applied to skin.

The US adult upper intake level is 1,000 mg/day and the EFSA supplemental limit is 300 mg/day [1]. Doses above 300 mg may interact with aspirin, warfarin, tamoxifen and cyclosporine [1]. Topical vitamin E products have been linked to allergic contact dermatitis [1].

angle.text: People take the gummies for general skin health. The link between oral vitamin E and visible skin change is a claim rather than a demonstrated result.

lead: Vitamin E gummies are a chewable form of a fat-soluble vitamin. Vitamin E is studied for skin health and ageing, but the article on the nutrient notes most studies found limited or inconclusive benefits and some potential risks [1].

The skin claims have a long history, mostly for topical products marketed for wounds and scars, which reviews have disputed [1]. The gummy trend applies the idea to oral supplements. The US recommended dietary allowance is 15 mg/day, and vitamin E is best obtained through a balanced diet according to the same source [1].

paras: Supplemental alpha-tocopherol above 300 mg/day may interact with aspirin and warfarin and others [1].
No studies found on vitamin E gummies. Studies of vitamin E and skin broadly found limited or inconclusive results [1].
